$comment: Kit config scaffold (conventions: commands.* are npm script names (e.g. build), not commands - install and sync refuse a value like "npm run build" (commands.lintStaged is the one full command); commands.dev is the npm script that serves the frontend in a slot (no such script = no frontend); slots.fePorts/bePorts are BASE port numbers (main = base, slot N = base+N); slots.fePortArgs are appended to the frontend start command, {port} = the slot's port, and must make the dev server FAIL when the port is taken, never move to another port - the default [--port, {port}] is only right for a server that already fails on a busy port; one that moves to the next free port needs its strict-port flag added (install and sync print a NOTE while commands.dev is set and every slots.fe* value is the default); slots.feExec (optional) runs that binary with npm exec -- instead of the commands.dev script; slots.feMatcher is a regex for the dev server's processes (default: run <commands.dev>); slots.feEnvFile (optional) is a local environment file the frontend needs - its slot copy (.local -> .slot) gets the slot's backend port; paths.srcRoot/serverRoot end with a slash when set; slots.dbNameFormat is a JS template body with ${n}; paths.hotspots is a list, rendered per context; project.i18nFile is a file, a glob or a folder (a trailing slash means everything under it), or a comma-separated list - every entry is an append-only hotspot; plans.openDirs lists the folders whose *.plan.md files are open plans - range folders like plans/300-400/ are never open; project.repoName is the repo folder name (default: the target folder name) used for slot folders and base hrefs; slots.dbBackupDir defaults to <project slug>-db-backups; paths.routesFile is the router config file; paths.planChecks is the project's own planning checklist that /plan's Architect + PM review adds when the file exists (optional; the kit never writes it); security.sensitivePaths: a regex string replaces ship-prep's built-in sensitive-path regex, a list of globs is added to it (and fills the Cursor security rule globs); tools.browser names the browser tool (left at the default, AGENTS.md does not name one); overrides is a list of { path, reason } for installed files the project keeps as its own - install skips them, sync reports them as override and never writes them; listing AGENTS.md there makes the kit write its rules to AGENTS.workflow.md, which CLAUDE.md imports). ci.install is the command CI installs the app dependencies with (default npm ci; e.g. npm install --no-audit --no-fund when the lockfile is not the project's to fix); ci.lintScope all runs npm run <commands.lint>, changed runs ESLint on the changed *.ts *.tsx *.js *.jsx *.mjs *.cjs files only, kit-managed files left out (vs the PR base; a push compares with the commit before it); ci.appAuditMode enforce fails the security workflow on a critical production advisory, report writes the findings to the job summary and a warning instead (the kit-managed scripts/ dependencies are audited report-only: a kit release fixes them); any other value of the two modes is refused by install and sync; paths.serverRoot empty = no backend job or step in CI; stack.conventionsDoc, backendDoc, styleSkill, authSkill, docsMapSkill, docsMapCheck, cssSection, componentsSection are the pack contract - a stack pack fills them from its pack.json provides (a project may set its own) and core leaves out what is unset. Core files reference these keys as {{dotted.key}}. Values here are placeholders; each project fills its own. Generic defaults are kept only for git.mainBranch, the slot naming/count, slots.fePortArgs and the docs paths (paths.sharedDocs, paths.planChecks).
